reason:
Cause hard-cap at round 3. The review has three design-wrong findings: F19, F20 and F21. The round-3 fixer revised the decision record after the review, so I checked each finding against the record as it now reads and against the code.

F21 is answered. D1 now uses an exclude line that seedWeftArtifactExcludes writes through mutateGitExclude, which PATTERN-fabric-boundary names as the only exclude mutator. That seeding runs at junction wiring and in ensureWeftLockDirAt, which every records commit goes through before it stages.

F20 is answered. D5 now reads the landing commit back from the record only when that commit is an ancestor of the parent's head.

I recorded both rulings with `lym loom decision add --by arbiter`.

F19 is not fully answered. The fixer departed from the review's fix (a): D5 now rewrites the kept tip before each merge-in, except when the task tip is an ancestor of the parent's head. The code runs a merge-in again on every pass. Finalize.mergeAndGate runs on every pass of the run loop, including the retry pass, every resume after a gate halt or Stuck, and the locked pass taken again after a fixer session (internal/landingshed/finalize.go:376-379 and :915-919). After a hand squash or an adopter-first squash, the merge-in's own merge commit Tm is no ancestor of the parent's head. So a second pass rewrites the kept tip to Tm. Tm's merge-base with the parent then already holds the squash. If no other run lands on the parent in the meantime, the no-record rule finds no net change, and the row has no landing commit instead of naming the squash commit. This is the outcome F19 was raised to prevent: a search over a tip that Finalize's merge-in already moved.

The record still needs this fix. At the hard cap, an accept ends the segment and no run agent would carry the fix out, so I hand the stop on.
question:
Review round 3 of keep-landed-records is at the hard cap.

F20 and F21 are answered by the decision record as it now reads. I recorded both rulings with --by arbiter.

F19 (key landing-commit-no-durable-source, open since round 1) still has a hole in D5's kept-tip rule. D5 rewrites the kept tip before every merge-in unless the task tip is an ancestor of the parent's head. Finalize repeats the merge-in on a resume after a gate halt, on the retry pass and after a fixer session (internal/landingshed/finalize.go:376-379, :915-919). The scenario:

1. The task branch was squash-merged into the parent by hand, or by an adopter first.
2. The first pass's merge-in leaves the task branch at its own merge commit Tm, which is no ancestor of the parent's head.
3. A second pass rewrites the kept tip to Tm.
4. The squash search then finds no net change, and the row has no landing commit instead of naming the squash commit.

Which rule should D5 use for the kept tip? Two options:

(a) Keep the review's rule: take the task tip once, before Finalize's first merge-in, and keep it across resumes. The fixer's objection is that this misses a merge fixer's later commits. But a fixer commit lands through a parent-side merge that makes a commit, and that commit names the landing directly.

(b) Keep the fixer's rule, with one more exception: never rewrite the kept tip when the task's tip is still the commit the last merge-in left. That commit is the merge record's MergeCommit, or its TaskHead when the merge-in was up to date.

Each option needs a matching D5 acceptance criterion: a hand squash, then a gate halt, then a resume, gives a row naming the squash commit.

Because the round is at the hard cap, the review segment can only be accepted (`lym loom circling accept keep-landed-records`). Either record your D5 correction with `lym loom decision add --by parent` before or after the accept, or order another round.
